nodes.name: Orographic rain
nodes.desc: Moist air rising up the southern slope drops its heaviest rain in the forest belt, while the northern slopes and alpine zone are much drier.

nodes.name: Cloud and mist
nodes.desc: Cloud wraps the montane forest and moorland, giving moisture to fog-dependent mosses and trees.

nodes.name: Snow and glacier melt
nodes.desc: Snow and ice cap the summit. Most of the ice cover has vanished since 1912, and the forest below acts as the main water reservoir.

nodes.name: Volcanic mountain soil
nodes.desc: Soils on the old volcano hold the nutrients that the forest and moorland plants take up.

nodes.name: Fungi, insects & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down leaf litter, dung and carcasses and return nutrients to the mountain soil.

nodes.name: Camphor wood
nodes.desc: A canopy tree of the wet southern montane forest, with ferns and epiphytes growing beneath and on it.

nodes.name: Tree heath
nodes.desc: Heather-family shrub forming the Erica belt of the moorland zone, above the forest.

nodes.name: Giant groundsel
nodes.desc: Giant groundsel endemic to the mountain, growing below about 4,000 m.

nodes.name: Giant lobelia
nodes.desc: A tall rosette plant of the high moorland and alpine zones, recorded very often in GBIF here.

nodes.name: Tussock grass
nodes.desc: Tufted grasses of the open moorland and tussock grassland above the tree line.

nodes.name: Eastern black-and-white colobus
nodes.desc: Leaf-eating monkey of the montane forest, with a Kilimanjaro subspecies. Its sloppy feeding also helps spread seeds.

nodes.name: Blue monkey
nodes.desc: Canopy monkey eating mostly fruit, plus leaves and insects, which are its main protein source.

nodes.name: Kilimanjaro tree hyrax
nodes.desc: Leaf-eater of the foothill and montane forest, reaching about 3,000 m on Kilimanjaro. Leopards and crowned eagles prey on it.

nodes.name: African bush elephant
nodes.desc: A mixed grazer and browser that disperses seeds. Elephants live between the Namwai and Tarakia rivers and sometimes climb higher.

nodes.name: African buffalo
nodes.desc: Grazer of the forest edge and clearings, listed among the park wildlife in the montane forest.

nodes.name: Common duiker
nodes.desc: Small antelope browsing leaves and fruit, seen above the timberline.

nodes.name: Four-striped grass mouse
nodes.desc: Small rodent of the open montane grassland and the most recorded mammal in the GBIF data here.

nodes.name: Garden locust
nodes.desc: A large grasshopper that chews grasses and other plants and feeds reptiles and birds.

nodes.name: Kilimanjaro two-horned chameleon
nodes.desc: A chameleon found only on the mountain that hunts insects.

nodes.name: Augur buzzard
nodes.desc: Raptor of upland moorland that mostly takes small ground mammals and reptiles, with the odd young hyrax.

nodes.name: White-necked raven
nodes.desc: Large crow named on the park page as a bird of the mountain; it scavenges carrion and eats insects.

nodes.name: African leopard
nodes.desc: The main large predator of the forest, taking monkeys, hyraxes and small antelope.

nodes.name: Crowned eagle
nodes.desc: A forest eagle that preys on monkeys and hyraxes in the canopy.
